titleEn: Splash at the Tub, Then Bread!

pages.text: "Hungry!" Lolo in yellow boots ran from the beach and grabbed bread. Dark handprints dotted it. "Lolo, what about your hands?" asked Riri in her yellow hat, but Lolo kept munching.
"Washing takes too long! I want to go out before the waves come in!" Lolo finished the bread and ran back to the sand. Sand grains on those fingertips mixed with bread crumbs.
A little later, Lolo's tummy rumbled. It ached, and Lolo rubbed it. "Mommy..." A tear slipped out.
Mom ran over, still wearing her blue fish-stall apron. She studied the handprints on the remaining bread. "Lolo, where did these marks come from?"
"Things much smaller than sand grains were clinging to your hands." Mom opened Lolo's palm wide. "They moved onto the bread and followed it into your tummy."
All three stood by the big wooden water tub in the yard. Riri spread three fingers. "I will count for you!" Lolo rolled up their sleeves.
"One, splash into the tub!" Lolo dipped both hands. "Two, bubbly soap!" Foam puffed up. "Three, rinse between your fingers!" Splash at the tub, then bread!
Lolo patted both hands on a towel, drying them completely. The tummyache had gone too. "Washing before eating means no tummyache!"
The next day, Riri brought a plate of bread. "Leave the bread there a moment!" Lolo ran to the tub first. Splash, bubbles, rinse! Now Lolo could do it all alone.
Mom held both Lolo's hands and pulled Lolo into a hug. Eating with washed hands left both tummy and heart comfortable. "Splash at the tub, then bread!" Lolo took a big bite.
